articles.title: MLB playoffs 2026: Division series preview, X-factors, predictions and more for Braves-Dodgers, Padres-Brewers, Yankees-Rays and White Sox-Guardians
articles.summary: All four best-of-five series begin Saturday.
articles.body:
Four postseason teams are out. Eight contending teams remain. It's on to the division series.

All four best-of-five series begin Saturday. Let's break it down.

No. 6 Chicago White Sox vs. No. 2 Cleveland Guardians

White Sox : Chicago entered the year as the ultimate underdog, with preseason playoff odds of approximately 1%, according to most projection systems. But the White Sox demonstrated early on that they were no longer in rebuild mode and instead ready to compete in the wide-open American League. Even when Chicago got swept opening weekend in Milwaukee by a combined score of 29-10, Brewers manager Pat Murphy went out of his way to heap praise on the opponent, foreseeing the White Sox as legitimate contenders in the AL Central.

Murphy was onto something: The White Sox spent the majority of the season at or near the top of the division standings, ultimately coming up just short behind Cleveland but still snagging the final wild-card spot. And after taking care of business with a two-game sweep in the wild-card series in Houston , the White Sox have guaranteed themselves at least one postseason home game for a fan base that surely did not expect to be hosting in October this year. Plus, Chicago has a chance at revenge against the Guardians club that chased them down for the division title.

Guardians : It was another scorching September for the Guardians, who struggled to find momentum early on and fell five games below .500 as late as Aug. 19 before catching fire down the stretch, surpassing the White Sox and claiming their seventh AL Central crown in the past 11 seasons. Aiding Cleveland's strong second half was its uncharacteristically aggressive trade deadline, which featured the addition of two veteran bats in Jo Adell and Nathaniel Lowe, plus an All-Star starting pitcher in Foster Griffin, who has helped stabilize the rotation.

But the real story of Cleveland's season is its terrific rookie class, headlined by left-hander Parker Messick, who is slated to start Game 1 on Saturday, and a pair of lefty bats in Chase DeLauter and Travis Bazzana. These consequential contributors have helped mask a frustrating campaign for face of the franchise José Ramírez, who missed more than a month due to a hamate injury and has rarely looked like his All-Star self for prolonged stretches this season.

The Guardians are typically much younger than their competition in the postseason, but their first opponent this year is similarly built — Chicago's rookie class is also stacked — which should make for an extremely fun series filled with young talent announcing themselves in the postseason for the first time.

It'd be understandable to highlight hitters with extreme boom-or-bust profiles such as Munetaka Murakami and Colson Montgomery, but I'm more inclined to keep the focus on Chicago's best overall bat. Miguel Vargas was one of just three hitters in the majors this season to hit 30 homers and 30 doubles and draw 100 walks, along with James Wood and Yordan Alvarez, and his sterling underlying metrics indicate that this breakout season was no fluke. Vargas also performed well against the Guardians this year, hitting .304/.424/.565 with three homers and more walks (11) than strikeouts (10) across 13 games. In a lineup filled with rookies and high-whiff hitters, Vargas needs to provide consistent quality at-bats, especially against Cleveland's best arms.

Because they earned the bye, the Guardians are in excellent shape with their pitching plans, as top arms Messick and Gavin Williams could combine to cover Games 1, 2, 4 and 5 on regular rest. But it'll be fascinating to see whom the Guardians give the ball for Game 3 in Chicago in front of what promises to be a raucous Rate Field crowd. Manager Stephen Vogt said Thursday that they're still working through their options, and Cleveland could go a few different directions.

Opening Day starter Tanner Bibee has made five postseason starts the previous two seasons, but he took a step back this season and posted a 7.36 ERA in September. Griffin has delivered some gems but also some clunkers since arriving at the deadline. Lefty Joey Cantillo has also been hot-and-cold for much of the year, though he has dominated more recently when entering the game following an opener. You can talk yourself into (or out of) any of these options, and it might depend on how the first couple games unfold, but this is a storyline to watch for Cleveland.

White Sox : The long ball can carry teams a long way in the postseason, and in this matchup, Chicago has the obvious edge in the home run department. The White Sox finished fifth in MLB in homers this season, with 211; the Guardians went deep only 162 times, which ranked 27th. Murakami, Montgomery and Vargas all hit 30-plus homers, while Cleveland's home run leader was Angel Martinez with just 18. The Guards proved down the stretch that they can score runs consistently without outlier slugging — and deadline addition Adell is a credible home run threat — but the Sox undeniably have more of a knack for clearing the fence. Heck, even Chase Meidroth is hitting moon shots lately, and if Chicago's lineup continues to build confidence, the Guardians' pitching staff could have difficulty keeping them in the ballpark. Those game-changing swings could prove to be the difference in a short series like this.

Guardians : Even with the question of the plan for Game 3, however you slice it, Cleveland enters this series with a considerable edge on the mound. Avoiding a third game in Houston was important, but the White Sox still asked a lot of their best arms across two wild-card games, including top reliever Grant Taylor throwing a career-high 54 pitches on Tuesday, Jordan Hicks appearing in both games and top starter Sean Burke throwing four innings Wednesday, which could render him unavailable for Game 1. Cleveland, meanwhile, can attack right out of the gate with two of the best starting pitchers in the American League in Messick and Williams and follow with a fully rested bullpen. And it's not just an advantage in the early innings; the Guardians also have one of the top game-enders in the league in Cade Smith looming on the backend. This collection of arms presents quite the contrast to the undermanned pitching staff the White Sox just faced in Houston, and it should minimize what Cleveland's offense needs to do to come out on top in this series.

These teams played each other awfully close in the regular season. The White Sox won seven of 13 games, and the aggregate score was 58-57 in Chicago's favor, with seven of the contests decided by one run and four ending in walk-off fashion. Those narrow margins suggest this series could go the distance, which makes me inclined to tilt slightly toward the team with home-field advantage and more experience navigating high-stakes October games. Chicago is fully capable of pulling the upset here, and based on how the season series played out, it arguably wouldn't be much of an upset. But I'll lean toward the Guardians here on account of that elevated experience and their advantage on the mound. — Shusterman

No. 4 New York Yankees vs. No. 1 Tampa Bay Rays

Yankees : New York finished five games back of Tampa Bay in the division but walloped the Red Sox in a wild-card laugher to set up a showdown of the consensus two best teams in a shallow American League. It was an emphatic, thorough performance from the Yankees offense, which scored nine runs in each game with an injured Aaron Judge off the roster and a compromised Giancarlo Stanton on the bench. The starting pitching was arguably even more impressive, with Cam Schlittler and Max Fried combining for 16 strikeouts and just one run allowed across 12 ⅓ innings of work. This team is rolling at the right time.

Rays : What a season it was for a Tampa Bay team that entered 2026 as most people's fifth choice in a stacked AL East. Instead, the Rays won 98 games behind a high-contact offense, a top-three rotation and the dream-stealing exploits of Junior Caminero. "How are the Rays doing this?" quickly turned to "Can they keep this up?" which morphed into "Will it work in October?" It's a legitimate question, considering the dearth of obvious stars behind Caminero. But there's also a chance that Tampa's crisp, low-mistake, fleet-footed style of play translates wonderfully to the high-stakes world of postseason baseball.

The glazy-eyed lefty provided the knockout blow against the Red Sox in the wild-card round with a high-arcing, three-run crank into the Yankee Stadium short porch. Boston had intentionally walked Ben Rice to get to Bellinger, and Bellinger made them pay. That's why, even if Aaron Judge returns for the ALDS, Bellinger will remain a critical character in the New York lineup. On a team full of high-whiff, high-strikeout hitters, the 2019 NL MVP is a much more Rays-coded character who can work a long at-bat and grind a pitcher down. Tampa Bay smothered Bellinger to a .520 OPS across 49 regular-season plate appearances this season. He'll need to be a bigger factor than that for the Yankees to win this series.

It's cliche because it's true: To win in October, you need special players to do special things. Caminero is exceptional for a multitude of reasons, the most important of which is his ability to clobber baseballs harder than almost anybody else on Earth. But Caminero's comfort in and thirst for the spotlight might elevate him to a whole other plane in this postseason. His dramatic, title-winning long ball in the Dominican Winter League a few years ago produced one of the greatest baseball highlights of all time. Most players want to be great; this dude wants to be legendary.

Yankees : By continuing to lean on their starting pitching. It's a testament to New York's outrageous rotation depth that the 2023 Cy Young and a dude making $27 million with a 2.67 ERA didn't get starts in the wild-card round. Expect Gerrit Cole and Carlos Rodón to feature prominently against Tampa Bay; one will probably start Games 1 and 4, while the other will slide to a Swiss Army bullpen role. Cam Schlittler, the presumptive AL Cy Young, will start Games 2 and 5. Max Fried will handle Game 3. The Yankees lost Game 1 of last year's ALDS in large part because they had to deploy a bullpen game. This team doesn't have that issue.

Rays : Everybody not named Junior Caminero grinds at-bats and gets on base. If the Rays can work pitch counts and get Yankees starters to the showers in the fifth or sixth innings, instead of the seventh or eighth, they'll get to pick away against New York's bullpen underbelly. It's difficult to envision Tampa Bay pouring buckets of runs on Schlittler, Fried and Co., but the Rays took the season series against the Yankees for a reason. This team can ball and won't be intimidated by the pinstripey-ness of it all. Expect The Trop to be rocking on Saturday.

It's impossible to pick against New York's rotation right now, considering how overwhelming it looked against Boston . I think the Rays will battle out a Game 1 win if the Yankees start Cole, but the Yanks will come roaring back behind Schlittler in Game 2 and finish things off in the Bronx. — Mintz

No. 4 San Diego Padres vs. No. 1 Milwaukee Brewers

Padres : If you didn't know why the Padres were the hottest team in baseball over the past month, look no further than their drubbing of the Chicago Cubs in the wild-card round . San Diego outplayed Chicago in every aspect of the game. That started with the production from its superstars, Fernando Tatis Jr. and Manny Machado. And backing up that offensive fire power, San Diego's pitching showcased its dominance as well. Right-hander Michael King shut down the Cubs' offense with seven innings of one-hit ball in Game 1, and the Padres' bullpen provided 5 2/3 shutout innings in Game 2 to put the series away.

Brewers : Another year, another season in which the Milwaukee Brewers' lack of marquee names doesn't mean a lack of success. Milwaukee steamrollered the NL Central, which has become a common theme in recent years. Among the things that went well for the Brewers was their dominant pitching, led by Jacob Misiorowski, who will likely be the NL Cy Young Award winner this winter. But it wasn't just pitching. The Brewers' offense was a juggernaut in its own right, ranking second in MLB in runs scored, despite ranking second-to-last in homers. And after finishing the regular season with a franchise-record 103 victories, the Brewers are looking to ride their successful year to an even better postseason, with hopes of making their first World Series appearance since 1982.

The Padres go as Fernando Tatis Jr. goes, but if there's one hitter whose impact could mean more in this series, it's Manny Machado. His regular-season numbers weren't what we're used to seeing from Machado in his career, but the Padres' franchise leader in homers showed in the wild-card round that he's still dangerous. If the Brewers are careful with Tatis, who is one of the best postseason hitters ever, that will leave Machado with opportunities to be a game-changer. And with one swing of the bat, San Diego's third baseman can swing the series in the Padres' favor.

If you're trying to slow down the hottest team in baseball, it helps to have the best pitcher in baseball. Jacob Misiorowski dominated the entire league during the regular season, and while it's harder for a pitcher to take over a series than it is for a position player, an ace like The Miz could. Misiorowski's start in Game 1 will be crucial for Milwaukee's success. If the Brewers' ace can set the tone in this series, it'll create a trickle-down effect for the rest of Milwaukee's starters. Misiorowski is the Brewers' engine. Their success in this series and the entire postseason runs through him.

Padres : San Diego showed in the first round that if its stars come to play, there's no stopping this team. And that's the Padres' most likely route to the NLCS. Milwaukee can't match San Diego's star power or firepower, and if Tatis, Machado and the Padres' offense do what they've done over the past six weeks, they'll run through the Brewers, no matter how well Misiorowski pitches. And with a bullpen that's the envy of baseball, the Padres can shorten any game and shut down their opponent, regardless of how their starters do.

Brewers : Neutralizing the Padres' stars is doable with elite pitching, and that's how the Brewers are built. Misiorowski and Logan Henderson keeping San Diego's hitters at bay in the first two games will give the Brewers the confidence to go into Petco Park and take this series. And with a bullpen that was third in ERA this season, Milwaukee can shorten games almost as well as the Padres. Offensively, Jackson Chourio has shown that he loves the big stage. With a 1.044 OPS and four homers in 12 postseason games so far, the Brewers' 22-year-old star is made for the moment.

This matchup has a chance to be one of the best series of this postseason. And with the hottest team in baseball meeting the team with the best record this season, it's a case of an unstoppable force and an immovable object. There will likely be big swings of momentum by both sides. Milwaukee's pitching holds the advantage, but San Diego's offense has the edge. In the end, the Brewers' ability to throw the best pitcher in the sport twice in the series and manage the middle games with its strong bullpen will make the difference. — Dorsey

No. 3 Atlanta Braves vs. No. 2 Los Angeles Dodgers

Braves : Atlanta bounced back from a deflating Game 2 wild-card defeat against Philadelphia with a resounding Game 3 win over their division rivals . Three shutdown innings from an improbable source, 32-year-old southpaw Ray Kerr, set the tone. Michael Harris II hopped on a first-inning Aaron Nola sinker for a three-run tank, and the rest was epilogue. The Braves head to Los Angeles feeling good, with their division rival and October bugaboo finally vanquished. A familiar foe awaits.

Dodgers : Baseball's new Evil Empire cruise-controlled its way to a 100-win season. As always with LA, it wasn't devoid of drama. Big free-agent signing Kyle Tucker sleepwalked through the first five months. Shohei Ohtani stopped pitching and then stopped hitting and then stopped playing. Edwin Díaz was a catastrophe. Freddie Freeman had one extra-base hit in September. But for all the hand-wringing and worrying about Los Angeles' roster of aging stars, they begin this three-peat quest with an extremely formidable group that includes deadline headliner Tarik Skubal.

Atlanta's main man didn't do much against Philadelphia, going just 1-for-9 with four walks and a single. The Braves probably can't afford to have Acuña disappear against Los Angeles' magnificent pitching staff. It has been said a million times, but Acuña having been sidelined for Atlanta's 2021 World Series run creates such a fascinating dynamic. He has a ring, but he doesn't feel like it's fully his, fully earned. And since his Game 3 grand slam against Walker Buehler in 2018, Acuña hasn't really delivered a signature October moment. The stage is set.

Is it reductive and overly simplistic to label Ohtani an X-factor? Perhaps, but this dude hasn't been a dynamic, intimidating offensive force for two months. He posted a .689 OPS from Aug. 7 to Sept. 7 while slogging through various physical ailments. Then he went on the IL for a stretch before coming back to go 5-for-21 across five games with just one extra-base hit. Doubting Ohtani feels like a fool's errand, but this guy has to physically decline at some point. There's certainly a chance we're seeing the beginning of that.

Braves : By getting meaningful innings from pitchers other than Chris Sale. The offense needs to do its part as well, but the longer series means the Braves won't be able to lean on their ace quite as heavily. How skipper Walt Weiss and Co. choose to navigate the games not started by Sale or Tyler Mahle will dictate this showdown. Atlanta has the bullpen to pull off this high-wire act, but it won't be easy, and more unsung heroes like Ray Kerr will need to emerge .

Dodgers : Lean, lean, lean on the starters and lean on the starters some more. Los Angeles won the World Series last season because its rotation rose to the occasion. That will need to happen again because this Dodgers offense is notably less intimidating than last year's group, at least on paper. Will Smith doesn't look like the same player. Neither does Freddie Freeman. We've already talked about Ohtani. Los Angeles wins this series by riding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow. It's not a bad plan.

Even if Chris Sale starts multiple games, the Dodgers still hold a significant pitching advantage. Yamamoto is coming off one of the greatest postseasons of all time. Skubal looks like a top-three pitcher in the world again. And then you have to face Blake Snell in Game 3. I'm definitely worried about Los Angeles' offense, but I don't think the Braves have the starters to take advantage of that particular weak spot. — Mintz

articles.summary: Tarik Skubal and Jazz Chisholm Jr. will play in the divisional round for the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Yankees, but it is very possible neither man will play for those teams next season.
articles.body:
Tarik Skubal and Jazz Chisholm Jr. will play in the divisional round for the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Yankees, but it is very possible neither man will play for those teams next season.

Find out the latest on those two superstar players, as well as what the future holds for Randy Arozarena, in this collection of insider reports.

Jeff Passan of ESPN reported on two-time Cy Young Award-winner Tarik Skubal:

"The number will be huge. Bear in mind that Skubal turns 30 in November and never before has a pitcher age 30 or older received more than Stephen Strasburg's $245 million (on a seven-year deal) in free agency. Provided there is no salary cap, Skubal could get double that."

Skubal has been the best pitcher in baseball over the last three seasons, emerging with the lowest ERA in two of those seasons and capturing the top prize available to pitchers in Major League Baseball.

According to StatMuse , Skubal has fanned the second-most batters since October 2, 2023, just behind Toronto ace Dylan Cease. His .717 win percentage is the highest during that period.

His 2026 was not as great as his previous two seasons, but there is little reason to believe the big lefty is going to fall off.

Considering the value of starting pitchers, particularly lefties, he is going to be the top target on the market this offseason. Whether the Dodgers can make a reunion work, or another team goes all-in on him, remains to be seen. Regardless of who lands Skubal, they will pay a pretty penny and for their sake, hopefully find themselves in the playoffs and competing for a World Series.

Prediction: The Dodgers have an uncanny way of getting what they want. If they want Skubal back, they get him.

Where Will Randy Arozarena Play in 2027?

Randy Divish of The Seattle Times reported, "It's long been assumed that the 2026 season would be Arozarena's last with the Mariners. He will be a free agent once the World Series ends, and he plans to test the market."

Arozarena was the best offensive player for a Mariners team that failed miserably to replicate last year's performance, which saw the team advance to the ALCS before being bounced by eventual World Series runner-up, Toronto.

The 31-year-old hit .281 in 2026, with 26 home runs, 79 RBIs, and 26 stolen bases.

There should be a significant market out there for a proven offensive commodity whose numbers speak for themselves.

The Atlanta Braves are an intriguing possibility and adding the left fielder to the squad would conceivably improve the the teams chances of being NL favorites entering next season.

Ditto the Diamondbacks, who are missing another bat to really push them over the top as a legitimate World Series contender.

Prediction: Arozarena signs with a high-profile, big-money contender, with agent Scott Boras telling the media, "Randy has made himself a lot of money this season."

The New York Yankees' second baseman has all of the natural talent in the world to produce at the plate and defensively, making him one of the more intriguing free agent options this offseason.

The 28-year-old delivered 109 hits, 19 homes runs, and 55 RBI this season for the Yankees, helping the offense produce in the absence of Aaron Judge through a large portion of the year.

There is reason for the Yankees would want Chisholm back, but Ryan Dunleavy of The New York Post reported that it is "common knowledge" that the team will not attempt to retain him this offseason.

The Seattle Mariners, who struggled with consistent production of offense in 2026, are a team that could utilize the flashy player. Ditto the Detroit Tigers, though one would have to question whether Chisholm and straight-forward skipper AJ Hinch would see eye to eye based on their clear personality differences.

Prediction: Chisholm signs with a contender, with Seattle being an attractive situation.

articles.title: MLB Won't Play Game at Grand Teton National Park After Exploring Idea, Rob Manfred Says
articles.summary: Major League Baseball has decided against moving forward with the idea of potentially holding a regular-season game at Grand Teton National Park in Wyoming.
articles.body:
Major League Baseball has decided against moving forward with the idea of potentially holding a regular-season game at Grand Teton National Park in Wyoming.

Johnny Flores Jr. of The Athletic obtained a letter sent by MLB commissioner Rob Manfred to Teton County officials. In it, Manfred noted that MLB had done "due diligence" on Grand Teton National Park as a potential site for a game, but ultimately opted to not pursue it any further.

"That said, since the story was reported, it has become clear the local community does not want us to continue evaluating Grand Teton National Park as a potential site," Manfred wrote. "We obviously would not bring a game to a community that has concerns about the venue, and will not continue to evaluate Grand Teton National Park as a potential site."

Jake Spring and Stephanie Apstein of the Washington Post reported Monday that MLB was in contact with the Trump administration about a potential game being played at a national park.

National Park Service Deputy Director Frank Lands reportedly scouted three sites within Grand Teton National Park to see if building a ballpark would be possible.

For the past decade, MLB has periodically held games at unique locations, including Fort Bragg in North Carolina, the Field of Dreams park in Iowa, Rickwood Field in Alabama and Bristol Motor Speedway in Tennessee.

MLB has also played a game at the site of the Little League World Series in Williamsport, Pennsylvania, every year since 2017, with the exception of 2020.

A national park would have been perhaps the biggest undertaking yet due to the amount of red tape MLB would have had to go through in order to gain approval.

MLB games are scheduled to be held at the Field of Dreams and Bowman Field in Williamsport next season, but no plans are in place yet for 2028.

Had MLB continued its efforts to bring a game to Grand Teton National Park, 2028 was the target year for it to happen, per Flores.

articles.title: Tarik Skubal's New Landing Spots Predicted by Insiders Ahead of MLB Free Agency
articles.summary: As Tarik Skubal prepares for his first postseason with the Los Angeles Dodgers, people within MLB are also looking ahead to his free agency and which team he might end up signing with.
articles.body:
As Tarik Skubal prepares for his first postseason with the Los Angeles Dodgers, people within MLB are also looking ahead to his free agency and which team he might end up signing with.

In a survey of MLB insiders conducted by ESPN's Kiley McDaniel , the Dodgers, New York Mets and Detroit Tigers were cited as the "true contenders" for the two-time AL Cy Young winner.

The New York Yankees were cited as being "just behind" the lead group in how often they were mentioned.

In the group of sleepers, McDaniel listed the Chicago White Sox, San Diego Padres and Los Angeles Angels as teams that frequently came up.

The Tigers, who traded Skubal to Los Angeles on Aug. 2, are the most interesting of the top group because they don't usually play in the deep end of the free-agent pool.

If they were going to sign Skubal, the Tigers could have just done it last offseason to avoid reaching the point where they had to trade him. He told USA Today 's Bob Nightengale during spring training there was "no offer" that came from Detroit.

The Dodgers aren't a surprise given Skubal is already there and they have a habit of signing the best free agent every year, but McDaniel did note the respondents had "some hesitation" about including them given the uncertainty around their ownership situation with Mark Walter at the moment.

Even though Walter sold his majority stake in the Los Angeles Lakers earlier this year just 10 months after his purchase was finalized, Dodgers officials have strongly maintained the MLB club is not being sold.

It will be interesting to see how aggressive the Mets want to be this offseason after a 74-88 record in 2026. They spent almost $240 million in free agency last winter, but fans were unhappy about the ways they invested their money.

Mets president of baseball operations David Stearns could also be feeling a lot of pressure given that he was at the center of a lot of vitriol from fans in Queens for things like not even attempting to bring back Pete Alonso before he signed with the Baltimore Orioles.

Among the three sleeper teams listed by McDaniel, the White Sox stand out as a team that could make a huge leap to being a top-tier AL team if they upgrade their rotation. The offense ranked fifth in runs scored and sixth in homers this season.

The Angels are in a fascinating position because Stan Kroenke is set to take over as owner after agreeing to buy the club from Arte Moreno for $3.9 billion.

Kroenke's purchase still has to be approved and the timing of that could impact how aggressive they are in free agency, but it's not uncommon for a new ownership team to want to make an aggressive splash right out of the gate.

The downside, though, is the Angels are so far away from being a contender after losing a franchise-record 100 games with a middling farm system , albeit one that is improving, that giving a huge sum of money to Skubal right now may not be the best team-building strategy even if it would make them more interesting in the short-term.

Skubal finished the 2026 regular season with a 2.72 ERA and 186 strikeouts in 158.2 innings over 26 starts between the Tigers and Dodgers. This was his fourth consecutive season with a sub-3.00 ERA and at least 10.0 strikeouts per nine innings.

articles.title: Freddie Freeman’s family stood by him through baseball’s hardest moments, shaping the Los Angeles Dodgers star’s journey on and off MLB field
articles.summary: Explore Freddie Freeman's inspiring journey with the Los Angeles Dodgers, highlighting the influence of his family's struggles, his son's recovery from illness, and his remarkable achievements in baseball.
articles.body: Freddie Freeman’s time with the Los Angeles Dodgers has been shaped by family experiences that go well beyond the game of baseball. The death of his mother, Rosemary Freeman, when he was 10 years old, made lasting changes to his childhood while his father, Fred Freeman, became an important figure in both his life and development as a hitter.Years later, Freeman would face another deeply personal challenge when his youngest son, Maximus, was diagnosed with Guillain-Barré syndrome in 2024. Freeman had to step down from the Los Angeles Dodgers due to the illness, but his wife, Chelsea Freeman and the family were focused on Maximus' recovery.Freddie Freeman’s family journey shaped his Los Angeles Dodgers career through loss, resilience and son Maximus’ recovery Freeman’s mother, Rosemary, died of melanoma in 2000 when he was 10. Her death was one of the major events of his childhood, with his father, Fred, continuing to raise the family’s 3 sons.Baseball also became a strong connection between Freddie and his father. After school, Fred would work with his son, making batting practice a daily routine. Their sessions helped develop the opposite-field approach that became a huge part of Freeman’s swing.Freeman has also kept his mother’s memory alive through baseball. His decision to play for Team Canada internationally has been linked to his Canadian parents and his wish to keep Rosemary's memory alive.Freddie Freeman supported son Maximus through illnessThe latest rough chapter for the Freeman family came in July 2024 when Maximus fell gravely ill. Initially diagnosed with transient synovitis, his condition rapidly deteriorated, and doctors started to suspect Guillain-Barré syndrome.The neurological illness was causing the paralysis to creep toward Maximus’ shoulders and affect his breathing. He was in hospital on a ventilator and feeding tubes while receiving intensive treatment. Freddie Freeman left the Los Angeles Dodgers on their road trip to be with his son and family.Maximus began to improve within days of intensive treatment. He eventually got out of the hospital, but his recovery involved learning basic movements all over again and continuing with physical therapy.Freddie Freeman and Chelsea honored CHOC caregiversThis experience of the Freeman family ultimately resulted in a major donation to the Children’s Hospital of Orange County, where Maximus was treated. In May 2025, after seeing the work of CHOC’s medical teams and pediatric intensive-care staff, Freddie and Chelsea Freeman announced a $1 million donation to CHOC.The donation comes after a particularly hard time for the family. Thanks to the hospital’s treatment, Maximus was able to come home. The Freemans then used their experience to help other children and families who are faced with serious medical issues.Freeman’s family story also became part of an extraordinary chapter in baseball. He returned to the Los Angeles Dodgers in August 2024 and played through an ankle injury in the postseason. Freeman hit the first walk-off grand slam in World Series history in Game 1 of the World Series against the New York Yankees.Freeman finished with 12 RBIs in the 2024 World Series, homering in each of the first four games. MLB also pointed out his six-game home-run streak in the World Series was a continuation of his 2021 postseason.But for Freeman, it was a year in which family circumstances had radically altered his perspective, which led to the baseball accomplishments. articles.title: MLB ABS Challenge Success Rate for 2026 Season Revealed, Full Rankings for Yankees, Dodgers, More
articles.summary: Now that the 2026 MLB regular season is over, the results for the first year of the ABS challenge system for all 30 teams are available.
articles.body:
Now that the 2026 MLB regular season is over, the results for the first year of the ABS challenge system for all 30 teams are available.

Per full-season data compiled by TapToChallenge.com (h/t Associated Press ), the Cincinnati Reds were the most successful team with a net gain of 16.8 runs on challenges. The Cleveland Guardians were last at minus-13.4 net runs.

Interestingly, eight of the 12 playoff teams ranked in the bottom half of MLB and had negative net runs totals. The New York Yankees finished 16th at minus-2.1; the two-time defending World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers were 26th at minus-8.5.

One of the primary culprits for the Dodgers' low rating was Shohei Ohtani with 5.5 projected runs lost in defensive challenges, just behind Seiya Suzuki of the Chicago Cubs for worst among all batters.

Jose Altuve was the most successful hitter with 5.6 projected runs gained on challenges.

Despite Cleveland's overall lack of success at challenges, Patrick Bailey ranked second among all catchers with 5.1 projected runs prevented. William Contreras of the Milwaukee Brewers was first at 5.2.

Per Baseball Savant , fielders were much better at challenging calls with a 58 percent success rate on 5,792 attempts. Hitters were slightly below average at 49 percent on 4,765 challenges.

Overall, there were 10,557 challenges that led to 5,686 overturned calls (54 percent success rate).

The Yankees and New York Mets tied for the most challenges won among all batting teams with 96. The Atlanta Braves have both the fewest challenges won (50) and fewest total challenges (120) among batting teams.

Among fielding teams, the Minnesota Twins led MLB with 157 wins out of 269 challenges.

The challenge system has already made its presence felt in the postseason. Game 2 of the NL Wild Card series between the Philadelphia Phillies and Braves ended when Phillies catcher J.T. Realmuto successfully challenged a pitch originally called a ball that wound up being strike three on Dominic Smith.

articles.title: Dodgers postseason primer: Where do Shohei Ohtani and everyone else stand as they go for a three-peat?
articles.summary: The Dodgers' bid for history features an enormous number of moving parts.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers' quest for a three-peat begins in earnest on Saturday with Game 1 of the NLDS , as they seek to become the first time since the 1998-2000 New York Yankees to complete a trilogy of titles.

Up to this point, the path for L.A. hasn't been entirely straightforward. There have been times when the Dodgers have looked a bit rickety, and that's to say nothing about everything happening off the field. They are also arguably the most talented team in the playoffs and are coming off another 100-win season.

No matter how you slice it, this is a club with more than its fair share of questions. Let's get into them, starting with the easier ones.

Who are the Dodgers playing in the NLDS?

The Dodgers will face the NL East champion Atlanta Braves , who defeated the Philadelphia Phillies in a three-game wild-card series . The Dodgers went 1-5 against Atlanta in the regular season, getting outscored 26-15.

The winner of the best-of-five series gets the victor of the other NLDS between the Milwaukee Brewers and San Diego Padres.

What will the Dodgers' postseason lineup be?

The Dodgers finished the season shuffling their lineup depending on the handedness of the opposing starting pitcher, and it stands to reason that they will continue doing so in the postseason.

Here's how they could line up against right-handed pitchers:

Shohei Ohtani has never hit in a batting order position other than leadoff in his MLB postseason career, but lately he has been hitting second against left-handers while Mookie Betts takes his old position atop the order.

Both of those orders alternate left-right all the way down to Edman, a switch-hitter at the bottom. It's entirely possible the Dodgers go a different route, too.

What will the Dodgers' postseason rotation be?

That's fairly settled. The Dodgers will trot out the quartet of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow. The order in which those arms are utilized remains to be seen, though the Dodgers have every reason to maximize innings for Yamamoto after what he did last year .

How has this season gone for the Dodgers?

It has gone well, by the standards of any other team.

By the standards of the Dodgers, well, there are a few dynamics at play. This is a good baseball team. They probably should've been better this season, and not just because they have the largest payroll in history, at a projected $410 million, per Roster Resource .

A two-time World Series champion filled its two biggest roster holes by giving two players, Kyle Tucker and Edwin Díaz, the highest salaries in the history of their positions. Entering the season, the Dodgers were estimated by the usually conservative PECOTA projections from Baseball Prospectus to win 104 games, and that didn't take into account acquiring a two-time reigning Cy Young Award winner in Skubal and more at the MLB trade deadline.

So in that sense, 100 wins is a disappointment. One of the most talented teams in MLB history (on paper at least) had more than its fair share of injuries, underperformances and mistakes. There was a point when the club seemed on the verge of letting the NL West become a race, as the Arizona Diamondbacks halved a division lead from 14 games to seven in the span of about a month between July and August, but then the D-backs got mired in their own slump and the Dodgers got hot again.

Overall, the Dodgers' issues boiled down to an offense that slumped hard in July and August, rough days for starting pitchers who will not be starting games in the playoffs and an epically bad bullpen night here and there. The first of those got better in September, though, which you can read more about here .

There is also the Dodgers' 38-37 record against teams with winning records this season, as their worst stretches of the year coincided with some of their toughest road trips and homestands, and that can leave an impression. Of course, it's a bit silly to worry about a team handling its business against good teams when it's going for a three-peat.

How does this team compare to last year's?

It's easy to remember the 2024 and 2025 Dodgers as juggernauts, but both of those teams had flaws that easily could've been fatal.

The 2024 Dodgers entered the postseason with a three-man rotation of Yamamoto, Walker Buehler and Jack Flaherty, with Clayton Kershaw, Glasnow, Dustin May, Gavin Stone, River Ryan and Emmet Sheehan among the starting pitchers on the injured list.

That team was so desperate for starting pitching help that it went full bullpen game while facing elimination at the hands of the Padres in the NLDS. It was only through the grace of a deep and competent bullpen that L.A. triumphed.

The 2025 team had the opposite problem. No one was doubting a rotation of Yamamoto, Snell, Glasnow and Ohtani, but there were most certainly concerns about a bullpen whose late-inning arms consistently blew games well into September.

Once again, the Dodgers adjusted. With their rotation overflowing, they turned to a number of starting pitchers to fill the gaps. Every single pitcher who appeared in Game 7 of the 2025 World Series started at least nine games for this year's team.

With that in mind, the 2026 Dodgers might be the franchise's most balanced roster to enter the postseason in years, but there is once again a major question.

Ohtani was the overwhelming NL MVP front-runner for the first half of this season, having begun the year as both a hitter and a pitcher for the first time in his Dodgers career.

Then Ohtani's knee started barking in July, resulting in the team taking him off the mound and giving him a lubricant injection during the All-Star break. He also developed a biceps issue at some point.

Those injuries didn't immediately stop Ohtani from playing. Much like he did in his recovery from internal brace surgery in 2024 and 2025, Ohtani played as the Dodgers' every-day designated hitter while rehabbing. However, the injuries clearly started to affect him in September, and the Dodgers opted to put him on the injured list for the first time in his tenure with the team.

Ohtani returned with five games left in the regular season and went 5-for-21 with 1 walk, 8 strikeouts and one extra-base hit, a double. Those numbers clearly aren't up to his standards, but if there's a reason for optimism, it's that he hit batted balls with exit velocities of 106.8, 106, 103.9 and 103.4 mph. He hadn't hit a ball that hard since August. Of course, the flip side of that optimism is maybe a 100% version of him would've hit them even harder.

Since his return, the Dodgers have insisted that Ohtani is feeling better, with hitting coach Aaron Bates saying Thursday that they had absolutely no concerns . The ship has sailed on Ohtani pitching again this season, though.

It still feels like Ohtani is the single biggest question for the Dodgers entering this postseason, given how long-term his knee issue has been. He at least got plenty of rest between his 15-day IL stint and the five days off between the end of the regular season and the start of the NLDS.

Do the Dodgers have a young, dynamic replacement at DH if Ohtani isn't healthy?

What an oddly specific question. The answer is yes, potentially.

It's not a stretch to say that Josue De Paula was the best hitting prospect in baseball at the time of his promotion to fill Ohtani's roster spot in September. At the time, every other position player in the MLB Pipeline top 10 was a shortstop who could offer significant two-way value, while De Paula will eventually be a bat-first corner outfielder at best and a bat-only first baseman at worst.

The good news is De Paula definitely looked like he belonged in his 11 games with the Dodgers while Ohtani was on the IL, slashing .323/.500/.581 and helping inject life into a previously struggling lineup. He was optioned when Ohtani came back, the timing of which made him available for the start of the NLDS.

In the playoffs, De Paula is likely to be the Dodgers' top left-handed bat off the bench, and he could fit in at designated hitter or corner outfield if someone gets hurt. It seems highly unlikely, however, that the Dodgers will take any plate appearances from Ohtani, barring a significant aggravation of that knee issue.

Those two players were the butt of jokes all season after they signed record contracts to join the defending champions, then posted the worst seasons of their careers. However, both offered reason for optimism in September.

Tucker entered the month slashing .228/.326/.357 but finished the season at .262/.354/.536, numbers more in line with what the Dodgers were expecting when they signed him to a four-year, $240 million contract. His six homers in September were double what he had in any other month of the season.

In 2026, Díaz made seven appearances with a 10.50 ERA, spent three months on the injured list due to loose bodies in his elbow, came back for nine more appearances, posted a 12.91 ERA in those, then hit the IL one more time in August due to what was described as neck inflammation.

Then he came back in September and, like Tucker, performed like the player the Dodgers were initially expecting, with nine strikeouts and one hit allowed across five scoreless innings. Díaz no longer has the closer role, but he made as good a case as he could for late-inning work in October.

Tucker and Díaz still finished the year with horrendous numbers, and barring some postseason heroics, that's what most fans will remember. Still, it's important to know that the Dodgers might not treat them in October like their overall numbers would suggest.

How's the rest of the Dodgers' bullpen shaping up?

It's a diverse group. We've already talked about Díaz, who could be anything from middle reliever to closer by the end of the postseason. However, the current closer is Tanner Scott, who played the Díaz role last year as the high-priced reliever who struggled in his first year with the Dodgers.

Scott's second season in L.A. has gone far better. He converted 25 of 29 save attempts with a 2.69 ERA.

As for the other six spots in the bullpen, the contenders are Edgardo Henriquez, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Kris Bubic and Brock Stewart from the normal pot of relievers and Roki Sasaki, Justin Wrobleski and Sheehan as overflow from the rotation.

Henriquez might be the most intriguing name from that group, as the flame-throwing right-hander was great during the regular season, only to hit the IL due to lower back discomfort in September. The Dodgers think he's trending toward playing in the NLDS .

Does a Dodgers World Series guarantee a salary cap?

You'd think. Some certainly seem to think. However, let's take a view rooted not in optimism but in realism.

The owners want a salary cap. They wanted one before Shohei Ohtani signed on the dotted line of a $700 million contract. They wanted one before Shohei Ohtani was born (what else happened in 1994?). They want a salary cap for the same reason every owner in sports has wanted a salary cap — not for competitive balance but to remove pressure on them to spend like they want to compete.

The Dodgers have made for a convenient boogeyman by being baseball's biggest spender and baseball's best team over the past several years. They must be stopped to save baseball, or so the argument goes, as no team is supposed to have L.A.'s combination of resources, competence and aggression. It's just not fair. It almost goes without saying in many discussions that the point of a salary cap is to end the Dodgers' unfair dynasty.

And yet, it really needs to be noted: Commissioner Rob Manfred does not fantasize about the Dodgers being forced to dismantle their tremendous machine — of Andrew Friedman, on his knees, begging a small-market team to take Glasnow's contract off his books — like some salary-cap proponents seem to do. Ohtani winning rings on the Dodgers has worked out quite nicely for baseball . A salary cap can be introduced for cost control and the veneer of parity, but MLB ultimately benefits from the large-market teams being contenders with the biggest stars. As such, it's hard to imagine a salary cap being introduced in such a way that the Dodgers, Yankees, Mets and other top spenders are forced to take immediate action to get below a line. A slow introduction of a cap or some sort of contract grandfathering seems far more likely, giving the Dodgers and others time to adjust.

The Dodgers' recent success isn't so much fuel for a salary cap as it is fuel for salary-cap opinions. It has certainly convinced many fans of a salary cap's necessity, but the MLBPA is playing cards at a different table. They don't want a salary cap, no matter what the Dodgers do, and they and the MLB owners are ultimately the people whose opinions matter here.

Limitations on the Dodgers would merely be a byproduct of MLB getting what it wants, and that would be completely antithetical to the history of the union. It's difficult to imagine the next month impacting salary-cap discussions to any significant degree.

What about the money problems with Dodgers ownership?

That's still in progress, and it remains unclear how much it will affect the Dodgers.

The short version of a very complicated story is that the companies operated by Dodgers majority owner Mark Walter were found to be doing business with one another at a rate much greater than what they were telling customers, investors and regulators. Walter is now facing considerable legal scrutiny and has reacted by selling whatever he can to pay off some of the loans that turned out to be less than kosher.

Those were big parts of Walter's sports portfolio, which also includes the WNBA's Los Angeles Sparks, the Cadillac Formula 1 team, the entire Professional Women's Hockey League and, of course, the Dodgers.

Dodgers leadership has repeatedly said the team isn't for sale . Of course, any sale would probably come out of nowhere — the Lakers' move was dropped on an otherwise uneventful Wednesday morning — but for now, that's mere speculation with the Dodgers.

One notable sign of trouble in Chavez Ravine, though, was a report that Walter recently approached Charter Communications about letting them out of their famously expensive Dodgers (and Lakers) contracts in exchange for a lump sum payout . It appears nothing has come out of that, but those are not stories you hear when everything is going well.

All of that's to say that Walter would likely welcome the immediate financial benefit of winning a third straight World Series even more than your typical billionaire. Of course, that outcome isn't up to him.

articles.title: Aaron Judge's availability for Yankees in ALDS vs. Rays still uncertain
articles.summary: Judge has been batting against live pitching and running, according to Yankees manager Aaron Boone.
articles.body:
Aaron Judge's status for the New York Yankees' American League Division Series matchup with the Tampa Bay Rays is still uncertain, manager Aaron Boone told reporters on Friday.

"We'll see," Boone said when asked about Judge's availability. "He'll be working out [Friday]. He hit again live [Thursday] at Yankee Stadium. He's doing more today over at [Steinbrenner Field in Tampa] and [Tropicana Field]. So we'll probably make those calls later tonight."

Asked if Judge had run the bases during his workouts, Boone said he wasn't sure but knew that Judge had been running.

The Yankees have until 10 a.m. ET Saturday to submit their 26-player roster for Game 1, which is scheduled for 6:30 p.m. ET in Tampa.

Judge hasn't played since suffering a calf injury on Sept. 16 and was placed on the injured list two days later. He was left off the Yankees' roster for their wild-card series versus the Boston Red Sox — though the Yankees didn't miss Judge in their two-game sweep, winning by scores of 9-0 and 9-2 .

One consideration in playing Judge at Tropicana Field is the ballpark's artificial turf. That could preclude him from playing the outfield if he's on the roster.

"It plays into it a little bit," Boone said, via the Associated Press . "But we're looking at the days, and so it's more is he going to be available at some point in this series, potentially, as a player? That's what we're kind of weighing and then seeing where he's at now these last few days, having taken live BP."

Games 1 and 2 at Tropicana Field are scheduled for Saturday and Monday. The series shifts to Yankee Stadium for Game 3 on Wednesday and Game 4, if necessary, on Thursday. Game 5 at Tampa Bay is scheduled for Oct. 10.

The Yankees could decide to have Judge on the ALDS roster even if he's only available to pinch-hit. If he can't play in right field, Ben Rice will likely remain at designated hitter. He batted 5-for-9 with 2 home runs and 6 RBI in the two wild-card games.

However, Rays manager Kevin Cash said he is proceeding as if Judge will be in the Yankees' lineup.

"I expect him playing right field, hitting third," Cash said, via the AP.

Gerrit Cole (3.61 ERA) will be the Yankees' starting pitcher for Game 1, while Drew Rasmussen (2.67 ERA) gets the nod for the Rays.

articles.title: Cubs' Jed Hoyer Reveals Top Offseason Priority After MLB Playoff Elimination with Padres Sweep
articles.summary: In one of the least surprising revelations of the still-early offseason for the Chicago Cubs, president of baseball operations Jed Hoyer knows they need to improve their pitching staff going into 2027.
articles.body:
In one of the least surprising revelations of the still-early offseason for the Chicago Cubs, president of baseball operations Jed Hoyer knows they need to improve their pitching staff going into 2027.

During his end-of-season press conference on Friday, Hoyer told reporters their pitching "has to improve" if the Cubs are going to be a World Series contender:

"From a pitching standpoint this year, it was sort of a struggle from the get-go. Overall, the quality of the pitching has to improve. The great majority of our focus [this winter] is going to be on pitching acquisition. I think we're in a good, remarkably healthy position on the position player side. I think that we have to focus our resources and energy on the pitching side predominantly."

Hoyer's comments come two days after the Cubs were swept in the NL Wild Card series by the San Diego Padres. Nothing went well for them in those two games, as they were outscored 12-1, but their lack of impactful starting pitching was particularly noticeable.

Matthew Boyd and Kevin Gausman combined to allow seven runs in 7.1 innings.

Hoyer tried an in-season fix for the rotation by trading for Gausman and Clay Holmes prior to the trade deadline. Neither player offered much help, as the Cubs' starters posted a 4.36 ERA from Aug. 3 through the end of the regular season.

It's especially notable that Chicago's rotation still finished in the bottom half of MLB in ERA despite having by far the best defense in the sport. The Cubs' 115 defensive runs saved was 28 more than any other team.

Hoyer also shouldered the blame for how he built the bullpen, leading to some of their late-inning struggles.

"I did a poor job in the bullpen this year, full stop," Hoyer said. "The guys we acquired this winter didn't produce nearly as well as they did a year ago. ... Some of that was based on injuries to some guys we were really counting on, but some of it was based on poor performance, some poor acquisitions."

The Cubs' 28 blown saves this season were tied for sixth-most in MLB. The Chicago White Sox (30) were the only playoff team that had more blown saves in the regular season.

Another reason Hoyer plans to target pitching is out of necessity. Gausman, Holmes, Boyd and Shota Imanaga could all become free agents.

Boyd has a $15 million mutual option in his contract. Holmes' deal contains a $12 million player option.

Those four pitchers accounted for 400 innings with the Cubs this season.

There is also some work that needs to be done with the lineup since Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki are also set to hit free agency, but Pete Crow-Armstrong and Alex Bregman will be back in 2027 to give the group a high floor.

articles.title: Red Sox’s Wilyer Abreu Gets Shocking Bargain $4.6 Million Contract Update
articles.summary: The Boston Red Sox have turned their eyes to the offseason. It’s earlier than they would’ve liked, but they were swept out of the AL Wild Card Series by the...
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox have turned their eyes to the offseason.

It's earlier than they would've liked, but they were swept out of the AL Wild Card Series by the New York Yankees, and so now they've got to think about what the 2027 campaign will look like.

There's one area where the Red Sox have the potential to be particularly busy in the offseason — whenever it can begin in earnest after a potential lockout — and that's salary arbitration.

They'll have a whopping 17 players up for salary arbitration, if they choose to tender them contracts.

One of the biggest names on that list is Wilyer Abreu, and MLB Trade Rumors writer Matt Swartz has projected values for all the Boston arbitration eligible players.

For Abreu, the number comes out to be quite the bargain.

The MLBTR projection for Abreu's salary for the 2027 season comes in at $4.6 million.

For a player with the power, glove and throwing arm of Abreu, it certainly seems like a massive bargain.

That doesn't consider everything that goes into arbitration, though.

Each player that reaches the major leagues via the minor leagues has six years of club control once they reach the majors.

The first three years have a salary based on the collective bargaining agreement, and they're considered the pre-arbitration years.

Years four through six of a player's time with a team are the arbitration years. In each of those offseasons, a player is eligible to go to salary arbitration to determine what he's paid the following season.

The arbitration process features the team submitting a value and the player submitting one, and the independent arbitrator comes to a conclusion on which one wins out.

Teams and players these days often negotiate in advance to avoid actually going to what can be a contentious hearing, but the value they come out with will still end up close to what it would've been in arbitration.

All that said, it matters which year a player is in for the sequence — and this is only Abreu's first arbitration year. Generally, the first arbitration year comes with the lowest salaries, and they rise in each of the two subsequent years, even if the player is viewed as having exactly the same value each season.

So for Abreu, no matter what he did this season, he wasn't going to end up with a giant arbitration value.

The Red Sox could always look to give him a higher-paying contract extension and buy out some of his eventual free agent years, but for now, Abreu is headed for arbitration.

The list of 17 Red Sox heading to salary arbitration is long.

The full list is: Tanner Houck, Johan Oviedo, Adley Rutschman, Jarren Duran, Eli White, Kutter Crawford, Connor Wong, Romy Gonzalez, Triston Casas, Andruw Monasterio, Zack Kelly, Greg Weissert, Wilyer Abreu, Erik Miller, Justin Slaten, Jahmai Jones and Tyron Guerrero.

If a team chooses not to tender a player a contract, they instead go right to free agency.

articles.title: Seattle Mariners Claim Former Local Top Prospect Off Waivers
articles.summary: On Friday, the Seattle Mariners claimed first baseman Michael Toglia off waivers from the Cincinnati Reds. Toglia went to high school in Gig Harbor, Washingt...
articles.body:
On Friday, the Seattle Mariners claimed first baseman Michael Toglia off waivers from the Cincinnati Reds. Toglia went to high school in Gig Harbor, Washington, so the Seattle Mariners give him a chance to come home for a fresh start. The Colorado Rockies drafted him in the first round of the 2019 MLB Draft after three seasons of college baseball at UCLA. In 290 career MLB games, Toglia hits .198/.275/.384 with 42 home runs across 1095 plate appearances. He has accumulated -3.4 fWAR in that period.

Despite his struggles at the major league level, Toglia still provides some intriguing power. In 2024, he hit 25 home runs with a slash line of .218/.311/.456. His expected weighted on base average was .361, which ranked 31st in all of baseball that season per Fangraphs (min. 100 plate appearances). Regardless, the lack of progress on those metrics in two hitter friendly environments provides some cause for concern.

Toglia no longer owns any minor league options, so the Seattle Mariners will have to designate him for assignment if he does not make the Opening Day roster. It is also possible that the Seattle Mariners will need his 40-man roster spot in the future pending future moves. For now, he provides some depth at first base entering the offseason.

Seattle Mariners Claim Michael Toglia Off Waivers

The Seattle Mariners lacked production at first base behind Josh Naylor this season. When Naylor missed time, Patrick Wisdom took at bats at first base, tallying one home run with a slash line of .106/.160/.191 and -0.6 fWAR. For perspective, Naylor himself compiled 0.6 fWAR the entire 2026 season in 152 games and 650 plate appearances. Wisdom only played 19 games and had 50 plate appearances.

Toglia was not much better in 2026 either though. In 10 games and 28 plate appearances, he hit .115/.179/.192 with an fWAR of -0.5. With this move, the Mariners are just hoping they can keep a local product around who has some previous success. He's much younger than Wisdom, so the likelihood of a bounce back is marginally higher, hypothetically. The reality is that Toglia may only be on the 40-man roster for a short amount of time. This is typical roster shuffling during the MLB offseason. However, that does not mean that the Mariners do not see anything in Toglia. They obviously acquired him for a reason.

Toglia Hopes a Return Home Can Revive His MLB Career

Per their scouting tool, Fangraphs gave Toglia a 60/60 raw power grade and a 60/60 fielding tool grade. Despite his low hit (30/35) and speed (30/30) projections, he still showcases great power at the Major League level. In 2024, his hard hit and exit velocity rates ranked in the 94th and 91st percentiles per baseballsavant . The struggle with Toglia has been his whiff rate; he does not make contact often at all. Yet, his chase percentage that season was only 58%. If the Mariners can get him back to swinging at good pitches, the hard contact is still there for some productive at bats.

articles.title: Brewers vs Padres NLDS: 3 ways Milwaukee can advance to the next round
articles.summary: Milwaukee has several ways to exploit San Diego in the NLDS.
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers enter the NLDS with the best record in baseball and a chance to turn a stellar regular season into a deep postseason run. However, the Brew Crew have their work cut out for them as they prepare to face the red-hot San Diego Padres in a best-of-five series.

Milwaukee finished the season 103-59 and earned home-field advantage throughout the postseason. The Padres will now travel to American Family Field to begin the series on Saturday, coming off a two-game sweep of the Chicago Cubs in the Wild Card round.

The Padres bring plenty of star power and an elite bullpen, but every team has weaknesses, and there are a few the Brewers should attack.

If Milwaukee is going to reach the NLCS for the second straight season, it will likely come down to exploiting these weaknesses and leaning on their own strengths.

Milwaukee should still lean on their elite velocity, because a Jacob Misiorowski fastball that tops out at 105 mph is going to be difficult for any batter to square up. However, against a Padres lineup that has handled high velocity well this season, the Brewers cannot simply expect to blow the doors off every batter.

As a result, Misiorowski's secondary pitches may become just as important as his heater. The same goes for the rest of Milwaukee's staff. The Brewers can use the fastball to work into favorable counts. In obvious fastball counts, though, mixing in some sliders and other breaking pitches could keep the Padres guessing and prevent them from sitting on velocity.

Milwaukee is second in MLB in runs per game in the first four innings at 2.27, and keeping this pace would go a long way against this San Diego team.

The Brewers must avoid turning every game into a battle of bullpens. The Padres' relievers, headlined by Mason Miller, are among the strongest parts of their roster. If Milwaukee can do damage in the early innings, they can put pressure on the softer part of the Padres' pitching staff before Mason Miller and the rest of the elite late-inning group take over.

If the Brewers could push a starter out after four or five innings, the extra wear and tear on the San Diego relievers could be significant in a five-game series.

Sep 9, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Milwaukee Brewers left fielder Jackson Chourio (11) during the game against the Chicago Cubs at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The Brewers' third key is playing offense "their way," by prioritizing contact hitting and placing constant pressure on San Diego's infield and forcing the Padres to make plays.

As the Brewers have known all year, hitting home runs is not the only way to generate consistent offense. Milwaukee led the major leagues in hits and batting average, and they are no stranger to manufacturing pressure with ground balls and aggressive baserunning (fifth in MLB in stolen bases).

The Padres' infield has had issues this season and, as a unit, collectively posted a -7 DRS (Defensive Runs Saved). Based on this statistic from The Fielding Bible , the Padres possess a below-average defensive infield.

If the Brewers can continue to create chaos, force rushed throws, and make San Diego's infield execute, they will be able to generate offense without relying on extra-base hits.

The Brewers don't need to change their identity to win this series. As long as they can keep San Diego off balance, attack the rotation before the bullpen takes control, and pressure the Padres' infield, they should be in solid shape to advance to the NLCS once again.

articles.title: Shohei Ohtani Gives Injury Update Before Dodgers vs. Braves MLB Playoff Series Amid Arm, Knee Issues
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani provided a positive update to reporters regarding ailments in his left knee (inflammation, soreness, lingering pain) and right biceps (discomfort, pain) on Friday, one day before L.A. will host the Atlanta Braves for Game 1 of the National League Division Series.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani provided a positive update to reporters regarding ailments in his left knee (inflammation, soreness, lingering pain ) and right biceps (discomfort, pain) on Friday, one day before L.A. will host the Atlanta Braves for Game 1 of the National League Division Series.

Ohtani hasn't pitched since July 3 due to the issues, but he's largely remained in the batting lineup, hitting .275 (.889 OPS) with 30 home runs and 81 RBI in 135 games.

Ohtani was placed on the injured list in September due to knee and biceps issues. He was out from Sept. 8-22 but returned for his team's final five regular-season games.

A big question remains about whether Ohtani, who has managed these ailments for months, will need further medical attention this offseason.

The knee issue first arose on June 11 , when he left a game against the Pittsburgh Pirates. Ohtani was removed from his July 3 start against the San Diego Padres due to the right biceps issue.

In the meantime, Ohtani may have benefited from five days of rest this week after the Dodgers, the National League's No. 2 playoff seed, bypassed the Wild Card Round.

Ohtani clearly feels good right now based on his comments, and we'll see how he fares soon enough when L.A. faces Atlanta for its 4 p.m. ET matchup.

articles.title: MLB: Los Angeles Dodgers to continue quest for World Series three-peat
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers will begin their MLB play-off campaign on Saturday, with the defending champions playing in a double-header live on the BBC.
articles.body:
Los Angeles has been the centre of the baseball world over the past few years.

The LA Dodgers have built a star-studded roster in Major League Baseball, winning back-to-back championships in 2024 and 2025.

Celebrities and royalty have flocked to Dodger Stadium, which will also host the Olympic tournament as baseball returns to the Games for Los Angeles 2028.

And you can get a glimpse of the Hollywood vibe as the Dodgers continue their quest for a World Series three-peat in the MLB play-offs this weekend.

After earning a bye for the first round last week, it is time for the Dodgers to join the post-season party and they will be part of an MLB double-header live on the BBC.

Saturday's coverage begins with the Chicago White Sox visiting the Cleveland Guardians for the start of their American League Division Series (18:00 BST).

You can then experience all the sights and sounds from Dodger Stadium, one of MLB's most iconic venues, as the defending champions begin their National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves (21:00 BST).

Opened in 1962, Dodger Stadium is the biggest MLB arena with a capacity of 56,000, and this year 'Dodger baseball' has been one of the hottest tickets in town.

For the past two years the team's total home attendance has passed four million. This year they set a franchise record of 4,034,219 - an average of 49,805 fans per game.

The signings of two-way star Shohei Ohtani and pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto in 2024 helped boost the team's Asian fanbase, increasing Japanese tourism to LA and supplementing the loyal local support.

Actors Brad Pitt, Will Ferrell, Bryan Cranston, Jason Bateman and Rob Lowe are all regulars at Dodger Stadium, while Justin and Hailey Bieber have been spotted at multiple games.

NBA star LeBron James and NFL quarterback Justin Herbert both attended last year's World Series, along with Sydney Sweeney, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle. Who will show up this weekend as LA hosts games one and two of the best-of-five series against Atlanta?

Having briefly been based in LA, Pierre Ducrey - sports director for the International Olympic Committee (IOC) - has also watched numerous games at Dodger Stadium and is "quite familiar with the atmosphere it can deliver".

"There's so many Dodger fans and they're very passionate about the team," he told BBC Sport. "They have an incredible venue and one thing I do know about baseball is this is the perfect home for a baseball tournament."

Ohtani rewrites history to send Dodgers to World Series

Why 'face of baseball' is on cusp of global stardom

The Dodgers aren't the only show in town. The LA Lakers are one of the biggest franchises in basketball's NBA, as are the LA Rams in American football's NFL.

The Rams won the Super Bowl in their own stadium in 2022 and are favourites to win the NFL's championship game when it returns to SoFi Stadium next February.

The stadium hosted eight World Cup games last summer and anticipation is growing that LA is set for a third straight World Series later this month.

"This is a city that lives and breathes sport and the Dodgers are a perfect example of that," said Ducrey. "The popularity of the franchise in LA cannot be underestimated."

Live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app

The Dodgers secured the second seed in the National League after finishing the regular season with 100 wins and 62 losses.

The Milwaukee Brewers were the only MLB team with a better record (103-59) yet the Dodgers are favourites to win the World Series, ahead of the Brewers and New York Yankees.

The Dodgers have continued to make big-name signings, with pitcher Tarik Skubal the latest in a mid-season trade, and their recent success has got fans dreaming of the franchise's first-ever three-peat.

"The Dodgers are in a very good period," Ducrey added. "There is a big momentum for them, but the team would still be immensely followed whether they're successful or not.

"There's a very long history behind it, and a very big tradition for baseball in Los Angeles."

Although Ohtani is a rare two-way player, the Dodgers' leading home-run hitter will not pitch again this year because of injuries.

Skubal is expected to start on Saturday and face Matt Olson, who led Atlanta with 41 home runs in the regular season and added another in Thursday's series-clinching win over the Philadelphia Phillies.

Either the Dodgers or the Braves will face Milwaukee or the San Diego Padres in the National League Championship Series (NLCS) - one step from the World Series.

Sixth seed Chicago have already upset the Houston Astros in the other half of the play-offs and either the White Sox or Cleveland will face the Tampa Bay Rays or Yankees in the American League Championship Series (ALCS).

The winners of the ALCS and NLCS will meet in the World Series, which is scheduled to begin on Friday, 23 October.
