articles.title: Breaking Down MLB World Series 2026 Odds For Final 8 Teams
articles.summary: If you enjoyed the appetizer, it's time for the two best National League and American League teams to return from first-round byes and join in on the playoff action.
articles.body:
If you enjoyed the appetizer, it's time for the two best National League and American League teams to return from first-round byes and join in on the playoff action.

That quartet of clubs are the 98-64 Tampa Bay Rays, 85-77 Cleveland Guardians, 103-59 Milwaukee Brewers and 100-62 Los Angeles Dodgers.

Before the four divisional series begin, let's take a look at the odds for the final eight MLB teams standing during the 2026 season.

A magical season for the White Sox continued with a two-game sweep of the Houston Astros in the ALWCS, with Chase Meidroth driving in four runs in the pair of Chicago victories.

Considering they lost 121 games just two seasons ago, the White Sox have been playing with house money for a long time now. This offense has enough talent to have staying power, both in this postseason and moving forward. In addition to Meidroth, there's quite a bit to like about Miguel Vargas, Tristan Peters and Munetaka Murakami, among others.

It's fair to wonder if the White Sox will be able to compete with the starting pitching that the Guardians have, but they've already done quite a bit that wasn't expected of them in 2026, so you can't count out Will Veneable's squad.

Even though they only won 85 games, the Guardians not only captured the AL Central title, but earned a first-round bye in what was a historically-weak junior circuit. There's no reason to think Stephen Vogt's club couldn't wind up in the World Series.

Parker Messick and Gavin Williams are a strong one-two punch in the starting rotation, while some combination of Tanner Bibee, Joey Cantillo and Foster Griffin could give the Guards one of the deeper rotations in the postseason. And if the Guardians starter hands the ball off with the lead, there's a good chance that a bullpen led by Cade Smith, Hunter Gaddis, Erik Sabrowski and Tim Herrin isn't going to give it up.

The biggest question for the Guardians will be their offense. Steven Kwan had a resurgence after the All-Star Break, batting .353 in the second half. However, José Ramírez posted just a .508 OPS in September, not looking all the way back from a left hamate injury. Cleveland is going to need the six-time Silver Slugger Award to heat up in the postseason if they're going to make a run.

The Padres parlayed an 18-6 month of September into a pretty dominant two-game sweep of the Chicago Cubs in the NLWCS. Will they be able to stay hot against the Brewers—who won a franchise-record 103 games during the regular season—in the NLDS?

San Diego will have their work cut out with likely NL Cy Young Award winner Jacob Misiorowski in Game 1, but there's reason to think this group will present a tough test for Milwaukee's pitching staff. Fernando Tatis Jr. posted a .996 OPS in the second half of the season, while Jackson Merrill wasn't too far behind at .909. Future Hall of Famer Manny Machado didn't have a good season by his standards, but it's encouraging that he went 3-for-7 with a home run in San Diego's sweep of Chicago.

It remains fair to wonder whether the Padres have the starting pitching depth behind Michael King to make a deep playoff run. But they have about as good of a bullpen as any team in recent memory, meaning if you aren't ahead of the Padres after five innings, it's going to be hard to beat Mason Miller, Adrián Morejón and company.

Every MLB Team's Biggest Surprise and Disappointment ⚾

For the second season in a row, the Brewers led baseball in wins. This year, they set a new high watermark for the franchise, winning 103 regular season games. But with continued success, just getting to the postseason is no longer good enough for Pat Murphy's squad.

Jacob Misiorowski was the best pitcher in baseball this year, with the likely NL Cy Young Award winner lead ing all MLB starters in ERA (1.80), ERA+ (232), FIP (2.17), WHIP (0.802), K/9 (13.0) and strikeouts (252). It would be easy to think this is just the beginning of a legendary career for the 24-year-old, but he averaged 100.6 mph on his fastball this season. Who knows how long his peak will be, and whether he'll remain in Milwaukee for all of it. The Brewers need to strike while the iron is hot with Misiorowski.

There's also reason to be urgent in the lineup. 2027 will be a contract year for catcher William Contreras, and if recent history is any indication, the Brewers will consider trading him in the offseason. Jake Bauers will be a free agent after a career-year that saw him hit 26 homers, drive in 86 runs and post an .874 OPS.

Is there enough starting pitching after Misiorowski? Can Trevor Megill rebound from a tough September? We're going to start to find out Saturday, with the Brewers hosting the red-hot San Diego Padres. Anything less than the franchise's first World Series appearance since 1982 will be a disappointing outcome.

The Rays have been to the World Series twice in franchise history (2008 and 2020). In such a weak AL, there's no reason that this shouldn't be the third time, and that this time Kevin Cash's squad couldn't get over the hump and win the first title in club history.

Tampa Bay's offense is led by Junior Caminero, who swatted 42 homers and drove in 101 runs this year. AL hits leader Yandy Díaz and Jonathan Aranda give the Rays a strong big three in their lineup.

The starting rotation could prove to be an even bigger strength. Drew Rasmussen (16-5, 2.67 ERA), Nick Martinez (15-6, 3.10 ERA) and Griffin Jax (8-10, 3.53 ERA) were already a strong trio in the rotation. Freddy Peralta's resurgence in September—a month where he posted a 0.96 ERA across five starts—might be a gamechanger that allows Cash to utilize a starter or two out of the bullpen, particularly in a short series.

And if the Rays have a lead heading into the ninth, Bryan Baker—41 saves, 1.44 ERA over 65 games—is probably going to shut the door.

It would hardly be a shock if the Rays hang a pennant or two this October.

The Yankees made quick work of the Boston Red Sox in the ALWCS, with Cam Schlittler (10 strikeouts over 6.1 innings pitched in Game 1), Ben Rice (two homers, six RBI) and Cody Bellinger (one homer, four RBI) all having big series.

Still, to defeat the Rays and have a chance to win their first World Series title since 2009, the Yankees are going to need Aaron Judge to return. The three-time AL MVP was left off the ALWCS as he battled a right calf strain. Whether Judge—who was limited to just 66 games this season—can play or not may determine the outcome of this series:

Also worth watching is what the Yankees get out of starters not named Schlittler, who is expected to start Game 2. Former AL Cy Young Award winner Gerrit Cole was good, but not great in his first season back from Tommy John surgery, as he posted a 3.61 ERA and 3.93 FIP in 22 starts. Meanwhile, Max Fried has a 5.03 ERA across 82.1 innings pitched, so he has to get the monkey off his back a bit.

The AL is as wide open as it's ever been, which has led to a sense for much of the year that the Yankees will ultimately return to the World Series for the second time in three years. But there's a lot that needs to come together for Aaron Boone's squad.

Particularly if Ozzie Albies and Austin Riley are going to play big roles like they did in a three-game NLWCS win over the Philadelphia Phillies , the Braves have the offense to make a deep playoff run.

Between Matt Olson, Drake Baldwin, Ronald Acuña Jr. and Michael Harris II, the Braves lineup is already pretty imposing. It's a great sign that Albies and Riley each delivered big hits in the NLWCS after disappointing regular seasons.

Atlanta is probably going to need to outhit the Los Angeles Dodgers—and any other future opponents—to win a title this year. Future Hall of Famer Chris Sale remains at the height of his powers, but he's only one guy. Tyler Mahle has been tremendous since being acquired from the San Francisco Giants midseason, although he felt an abdominal pull before making a strong Game 2 outing, so his health is worth monitoring.

In the bullpen, Raisel Iglesias and Didier Fuentes are a strong one-two punch, but the Braves will need a rebound from Dillon Lee, who gave up back-to-back homers to Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper in Game 2. Also, Robert Suarez is likely going to need to play a bigger role for the Braves than he did in their opening postseason series.

The Dodgers are looking to become the first team to win three World Series titles in a row since the Yankees did it from 1998-2000. They'll enter their NLDS matchup with the Braves favored to win it all again.

Two-time defending AL Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal is now at the forefront of a rotation that includes reigning World Series MVP Yoshinobu Yamamoto, two-time Cy Young Award winner Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow. Last year, the rotation for the Dodgers came together in a manner that allowed them to win the World Series without much of a bullpen, because their starters both pitched deep into games and took down some relief innings. Will that happen again in 2026?

Four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani won't pitch, but he'll still be at DH, looking to maintain the .940 career postseason OPS he has. Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts, Kyle Tucker, Max Muncy, Teoscar Hernández, Will Smith and Miguel Rojas are among the other players on Dave Roberts' roster with a history of big hits in the postseason. And don't forget, this is the time of the year where Kiké Hernández becomes Barry Bonds.

When you look at the roster, it's hard to pick anyone over the Dodgers. But they learned last year just how hard it is to repeat, and three-peating is even more difficult. Recent history suggests that the best time to knock the Dodgers off is in the NLDS when they are a little rusty after the bye.

articles.title: Who Will Win Each MLB Playoffs Division Series?
articles.summary: While eight Wild Card teams were busy knocking each other out this week, four sleeping giants of the Major League Baseball season have been watching. It’s ti...
articles.body:
While eight Wild Card teams were busy knocking each other out this week, four sleeping giants of the Major League Baseball season have been watching.

It's time for the Division Series of the 2026 MLB Postseason . 100-win tyrants, darlings, division matchups, MVPs. Eight of baseball's best square up in the brief yet explosive best-of-five series.

Via FanGraphs , on Opening Day , the Cleveland Guardians and Chicago White Sox had an 8.7% and 0.6% chance to win the AL Central, respectively. That was good for fourth and fifth place.

All year long, Chicago led the division while the Guardians stayed within a few games. That changed during a series between the two in September, when Cleveland took first and held it.

That pushed the White Sox to finish in the Wild Card. They swiftly took care of the Houston Astros in two games this week.

So the division foes, who nobody predicted to be here, now face off for a spot in the ALCS.

Chicago's lineup showed up and showed out in Houston, scoring a combined seven runs in the first two innings. The Astros were just never able to catch up, and if Chicago replicates that, this series could be over quickly.

However, the White Sox are facing an exponentially better pitching staff than the Astros'. The Guardians ended with the ninth-best starting pitcher ERA and sixth-best bullpen ERA in baseball. Houston was 27th and 18th, respectively.

This five-game series will come down to the White Sox lineup. In the 13 games they played this season, Chicago plated 4.5 runs per game. That mark would be enough to win this series.

Cleveland's offense scored the 24th most runs per game and sits in the basement of team average, SLG and OPS. Although they have every pitching advantage over Chicago, teams need to hit home runs to win playoff games in 2026. And home runs are where the White Sox excel.

Don't expect the scoring Chicago piled on in Houston, but the brand of baseball the Sox are playing should send them into the league Championship Series.

There is no bigger target on the back of a team right now than the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Back-to-back World Series, a $380 million payroll and potentially the biggest component of MLB's looming labor lockout.

LA welcomes in a team that's watched them beat the Dodgers all year long: the Atlanta Braves.

In the six games between the Dodgers and Braves this year, Atlanta's won five.

The Braves survived an elimination game against the Philadelphia Phillies on Thursday, but played an overall good series. Everything they did to win 94 games and win the National League East, they did in the Wild Card.

Starting pitching was phenomenal, and the threat of every guy in the Braves lineup to strike, struck. But you

can't talk about the danger of a deep lineup and not talk about the Dodgers.

Los Angeles does have the lineup and pitching staff advantage over Atlanta. But the Braves have shown they know how to beat the Dodgers.

LA enters having won seven straight playoff series. This is a veteran, experienced team that everyone is trying to beat. The Dodgers won 100 games in 2026, the most in their consecutive World Series wins era. The team has been injured a lot since the All-Star break, but has had everyone return through September and return well.

If the Braves want to win this series, they must score more consistently than they did against Philadelphia. They're facing a much better rotation and bullpen than the Phillies, and need a lot to go right to dethrone this giant.

With all of this said, Los Angeles is the better team. Atlanta might not have the legs to keep up in the extended five-game series.

The Tampa Bay Rays and New York Yankees have been the clear-cut best teams in the American League. Thanks to the playoff format, these two meet in the ALDS, and not the ALCS.

Tampa Bay finished with 98 wins and the best record in the AL. They also won seven of the 13 games played against the Yankees in 2026.

But New York's coming in red hot. Without Aaron Judge , the Yankees hung nine runs on the Red Sox in each night of the two-game sweep. The Yankees punched Boston in the teeth while flexing the muscle of their starting pitching.

The MLB-leading starting pitching. No team finished with a higher SP ERA than the Yankees, and nobody really came close. In a rotation with Max Fried , Gerrit Cole and Carlos Rodon , a 25-year-old will win the Cy Young over all of them.

Cam Schlittler delivered in his start against the Red Sox and has a career 2.58 ERA against the Rays.

No team in the league is harder to get outs against than Tampa Bay. The 2026 Rays have a league-leading batting average and never strike out. They don't stack runs on the board, but they don't need to. The Rays execute near-flawless small ball and have the best winning percentage in one-run games of all playoff teams.

This will be a tough series for the Yankees. Judge's health could be the difference between another disappointing ALDS exit and a damn good shot at the World Series.

Tampa Bay is coming in with a rested and healthy starting rotation, which isn't nearly as good as New York's, but can very well hold their own. Home-field advantage for the Rays will also prove vital, having won 68% of their games at Tropicana Field this year.

This is undoubtedly one of the better Yankees teams in recent memory, but facing Tampa Bay right now is difficult. If this were a seven-game ALCS, New York's starting pitching could outlast the Rays. But since the Rays are rested and at home, Tampa Bay should advance to the ALCS.

Bear down for the battle between the Milwaukee Brewers and San Diego Padres.

This is a matchup between the best team in baseball and the hottest team in baseball. San Diego disposed of the Chicago Cubs in two games last week, riding hot bats and their lockdown bullpen.

Fernando Tatis Jr. and Manny Machado are leading a Padres team with a different feel from last year's. San Diego is playing with deadly confidence and with nothing to lose. They believe they can beat anybody right now, and that may be the case.

San Diego handled the best team of 2026 in their six games played this year, winning four. The Padres swept the Brewers in Petco Park in August, but lost the series in Milwaukee in May.

Although nobody wants to play the Padres right now, that title belonged to the Brewers for all of 2026.

Milwaukee has made the postseason eight of the last nine years, but hasn't reached the World Series once. That said, this is the best Brewers team of all time.

They set a franchise record with 103 wins in 2026. They've been beating good teams all season long and have produced one of the better lineups and pitching staffs of the season.

This Milwaukee team also has something seven of the eight other Brewers playoff teams didn't. A 104-mph-throwing 24-year-old Cy Young, Jacob Misiorowski .

Misiorowski has been the best pitcher of 2026. He made 30 starts at a 1.80 ERA, striking out an MLB-leading 265 along the way. He spearheads a tremendous starting rotation with Logan Henderson and Kyle Harrison .

This Brewers team doesn't have the wow-factor (outside of Misiorowski's fastballs), but just finds ways to win. That said, this Padres team can beat anybody right now, and should advance through a thrilling series.

Game 1 of every series begins tomorrow, Oct. 3.

The Guardians and White Sox begin at 1 p.m. ET, and the final game of the day, Brewers-Padres, will begin at 8:30 p.m. ET.

The Wild Card round is fun, but the division series is where October baseball gets real and contenders are tested.

The Braves will get the first shot at knocking off the two-time defending champs. The White Sox have an opportunity to play for the World Series after losing 121 games just two years ago.

Two of the AL's best meet earlier than they should. And can the Padres really beat the Brewers?

All of those questions and more will be answered next week.

articles.title: Cardinals Acquire Young Strikeout Talent In Trade NL West Trade
articles.summary: The St. Louis Cardinals announced a 23-year-old trade addition after completing a deal with a National League West contender.
articles.body:
The St. Louis Cardinals entered 2026 with a clear emphasis on building a younger roster and creating a foundation for the next competitive window. The season uncovered some potential building blocks of the future, like Alec Burleson and Jordan Walker, and that process will continue into the offseason, with the organization looking for ways to add talent without abandoning its long-term approach.

"The Cardinals have always been clear on what 2026 was about: building toward the future," Josh Jacobs wrote for MLB.com . "The front office is unlikely to be ultra-aggressive in upgrading the roster with external additions ahead of next season. But there will be ways to upgrade the big league team while still keeping the future in mind."

That philosophy was evident again with a move that quietly kicked off the team's offseason as the Cardinals completed one of biggest trades of the summer, bringing another young arm into an organization that has increasingly prioritized pitching development.

St Louis Cardinals Add 23-Year-Old Strikeout Artist To Complete Deadline Trade

On Thursday, the Cardinals announced that they had acquired right-hander Brian Curley from the Arizona Diamondbacks as the player to be named later in the Lars Nootbaar trade.

The deal gives St. Louis a former third-round pick with a strong strikeout track record to work with as the organization continues reshaping its pitching pipeline. Curley was selected by Arizona in the 2025 MLB Draft after previously being selected by Pittsburgh in the 16th round of the 2024 draft.

Curley struck out 130 batters over 116 minor-league innings in 2026, producing an impressive 10.1 strikeout-per-nine rate. He also posted a 2.6 BB/9 mark, showing that his ability to miss bats was accompanied by manageable control.

St Louis Cardinals Continue Building Young Core With New Trade Addition

Curley's 2026 campaign was not without some concerns though. He finished the season with a 5.28 ERA and a 1.543 WHIP, including a 6.41 ERA over 46 and one-third innings at Double-A Amarillo. But the underlying strikeout and walk numbers provide an intriguing foundation for the Cardinals' player-development staff.

"Curley struck out 25.3% of batters faced this year," Darragh McDonald wrote for MLB Trade Rumors . "He only issued walks to 6.6% of them. He induced grounders on 43.2% of balls in play. Those are all strong figures. The ERA was likely inflated by a .381 batting average on balls in play. He also saw 21.4% of his fly balls leave the yard, about double a normal rate. Sometimes, a home run spike can be related to what a pitcher is doing but it can also be fluky in small samples."

Curley now joins a Cardinals organization that will be looking to add another strikeout-oriented pitcher to its near-term core. The move may not produce an immediate impact at Busch Stadium, but Curley represents precisely the kind of young, controllable pitching talent the Cardinals have been seeking as they build toward the future.

LOS ANGELES — After two days of four playoff games during the wild card round, Saturday gives us one more day full of baseball on Saturday to start the Division Series round in both the American League and National League.

The Dodgers will start Tarik Skubal in Game 1 of their NLDS against a potential bullpen game by the Braves, in the second game of the day, a 1 p.m. start at Dodger Stadium with temperatures expected in the triple digits .

"Hopefully everyone is drinking a lot of water and staying hydrated," Skubal said Friday. "It's going to be a hot one."

But the first game of Saturday is in Cleveland, with the Guardians facing the Chicago White Sox in a true division series. The other ALDS is also an actual division series with Drew Rasmussen and the Tampa Bay Rays hosting Gerrit Cole and the New York Yankees.

Saturday ends with Robbie Ray and the San Diego Padres on the road to face likely NL Cy Young Award winner Jacob Misiorowski and the Milwaukee Brewers at Miller Park.

Fox Sports has the NL playoffs this year, with TBS televising the AL side.

After Saturday, there's one more chance for a day with four postseason baseball games. If both National League series don't end in sweeps, next Wednesday, October 7 will feature two NLDS Games 4 and two ALDS Games 3.

articles.title: Aaron Judge not included on Yankees' ALDS roster to face Rays
articles.summary: Judge has been out since Sept. 18 and missed the wild-card round victory over the Red Sox.
articles.body:
New York Yankees slugger Aaron Judge will not play in the AL Divisional Series against the Tampa Bay Rays after he was excluded on the team's 26-man roster on Saturday.

Judge sat out the Yankees' AL wild-card round sweep of the Boston Red Sox due to a moderate calf strain. He was placed on the injured list on Sept. 18 and four days later manager Aaron Boone said the team was planning to play without Judge in the opening round.

"We feel like in a couple weeks since the injury, he's made real strides and significant improvements," Boone said on Wednesday. "Hopefully, we're in a position to make another decision in a couple of days."

Judge took live batting practice at Yankee Stadium on Monday and took more live at-bats at the team's Double-A affiliate in Somerset on Wednesday. He told reporters that he'd been limited to running on an anti-gravity treadmill designed for rehabilitation before running on the Yankee Stadium field before Game 1 of the Red Sox series.

One consideration in playing Judge at Tropicana Field is the ballpark's artificial turf, something that Boone said could have been a part of the decision-making process.

"It plays into it a little bit," Boone said Friday, via the Associated Press . "But we're looking at the days, and so it's more is he going to be available at some point in this series, potentially, as a player? That's what we're kind of weighing and then seeing where he's at now these last few days, having taken live BP."

The Yankees will travel to Tampa with the Rays hosting Games 1 and 2 on Saturday and Monday. The series will shift to Yankee Stadium for Game 3 on Wednesday and a possible Game 4 on Thursday. Should it be necessary, a winner-take-all Game 5 would take place on Saturday, Oct. 10 at Tropicana Field.

articles.title: Milwaukee Brewers are embracing the pressure and their youth as NLDS begins: 'There's a different feeling around the team'
articles.summary: The Brewers haven't reached the World Series since 1982. This team is hoping to change that.
articles.body:
MILWAUKEE — For years, the Milwaukee Brewers have been seen as an underdog — at least on paper.

It's easy to see why that narrative has hung around. The Brewers are consistently one of the youngest teams in the sport, and they play in baseball's smallest market. But this team has shown for the better part of the past decade that they're not to be overlooked. In fact, they've consistently been one of MLB's best. This season, Milwaukee not only had baseball's best record, but also their 103 wins set a franchise record.

And yet, despite their regular-season success, in the postseason, the Brewers have had their fair share of disappointment in recent years.

" Two years ago, we got beat by a ninth-inning homer by [Pete] Alonso when we had one of the best relievers in baseball on the mound," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said, referring to his team's loss to the Mets in the 2024 wild-card round. "So that happens. We had an opportunity to move on. We were right there.

"Last year, we ran into a team that was very, very hot," he said of the 2025 NLCS sweep at the hands of the Dodgers. "I think everybody would say that. They're not only hot, but they were super talented, super built for that. They played their best baseball that series."

This time around, the Brewers' test is not about talent. It's about getting over a hump that has stymied them for the past 44 years. Milwaukee has never won the World Series and hasn't been there since 1982, when the Brewers were a member of the American League and lost in seven games to the St. Louis Cardinals.

What makes this Brewers team different from other quality teams who failed to reach the World Series? Experience, for one thing. Much of this 2026 team was on the roster for the 2024 wild-card defeat and the 2025 NLCS sweep.

Even though Milwaukee is often one of the younger teams in baseball, going through the lows of disappointing playoff exits can bring a level of experience even in a short amount of time. And building that type of callus becomes its own advantage over the course of a 162-game season and heading into another postseason with high expectations.

"I think there's a different edge to this team," president of baseball operations Matt Arnold said. "They're bonded together in a really unique way. They're well-balanced in a unique way. And I think they'll be ready."

No matter how ready they are, there is no easy path for the Brewers to reach the Fall Classic. The San Diego Padres, whom they face starting Saturday in the NLDS , have been baseball's hottest team for the past six weeks. And getting through San Diego means a date with either the Atlanta Braves, who have been firing on all cylinders lately, or the back-to-back World Series champion Dodgers, who ran through Milwaukee last season.

But these Brewers don't talk like they want an easy road. In fact, they're using those past disappointments as fuel for what they believe they're capable of in the present.

"I think back to last year, I think there was an element of maybe a little bit of lack of belief that we could do it," first baseman Jake Bauers said. "Maybe a little too much doubt. And I think going into this postseason, there's a different feeling around the team.

"I think there's been a concerted effort to make sure that everybody in the room knows what we're capable of and that it doesn't require anybody to do something that they're not able to do."

It's hard to look at the Brewers' roster and not notice how young they are compared to other teams in the playoff field (outside the also very young Chicago White Sox). Ten of the 26 players on Milwaukee's postseason roster are under the age of 27. But the Brewers have the unique advantage of being both young and experienced. Star outfielder Jackson Chourio is just 22 years old but has already played in three full MLB seasons and two postseasons.

And he has already proven that when the lights are brightest, he can be at his best, with a 1.044 OPS and four homers in 12 postseason games.

"I don't think youth hurts us. I think youth helps us because these guys are forging their mindsets and creating their approach to the game," Murphy said. "I think youth in a lot of ways helps us. And I think that's been a key more than people know to have those young, hungry players.

"The year that the Washington Nationals came from the wild card to win it all, were they necessarily the best team? They were the best team at that time because of what they went through … And that's how it works. But I don't think the youth is an excuse by any means. I think, especially the way we play, I think there's a lot of value in having that youth."

There might be more pressure on this Brewers team than there has been on any Milwaukee team in a long time. But as they begin their journey to try to get back to the World Series for the first time in 44 years, that doesn't seem to rattle them. Maybe, in some ways, that pressure has even made them stronger.

"We've built a really good team, a really good culture, and I think we believe in each other," Bauers said. "I think we all know that whether one person doesn't get it done, there's someone right behind them that's going to be ready to pick them up. And that's something that we've done all year, and I think that's only added to the confidence."

L.A. entered the NLDS opener as 1.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , hoping to begin its quest for a third straight World Series title with a Game 1 win over the Braves.

Behind a stunning performance from Skubal that held Atlanta to one run and a barrage of home runs, the Dodgers delivered on those expectations, taking Game 1 at home and looking every bit like a team capable of making another run at a championship.

Teoscar Hernández launched a 431-foot, two-run homer in the bottom of the fourth to bring in Freddie Freeman and kick off the scoring after a pitching clinic by both teams' aces, Dodgers' Skubal and Braves' Dylan Dodd.

The Braves responded in the top of the sixth when Sean Murphy opened the inning with a 421-foot bomb to center field, cutting the deficit to 2-1.

The Dodgers were having none of that, adding two more home run punches from Kyle Tucker and Max Muncy in the bottom of the sixth to bring in three runs.

In a last-ditch effort by the Braves in the top of the ninth, Ozzie Albies homered to center field with no outs, bringing in two runs to cut the deficit to 5-3.

With a runner on second and two outs, Austin Riley grounded out to shortstop, ending a near-comeback by the Braves.

Game 2 will remain in Los Angeles on Sunday, with first pitch scheduled for 8 p.m. ET and available to watch on FS1.

articles.summary: Tarik Skubal dominated on the mound while Kyle Tucker and Teoscar Hernández launched massive home runs to power the Los Angeles Dodgers over the Atlanta Braves for the Game 1 win.

For the Atlanta Braves, it was a bullpen game, while the Los Angeles Dodgers sent out two-time American League Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. On Saturday afternoon at Dodger Stadium, the elite starting pitcher led the way. Skubal was dominant, striking out seven hitters while allowing one run on two hits and two walks over six innings of work in the Dodgers' 5-3 Game 1 NLDS win. The Dodgers began their quest for a third straight World Series title with a statement win over the Braves, but the game didn't start off smoothly. articles.title: Tarik Skubal retires 15 straight Braves batters in first Dodgers playoff start, backed by 3 homers in Game 1 NLDS win
articles.summary: Skubal was dynamite for much of the scorching afternoon in Los Angeles.
articles.body: On a day when temperatures reached triple digits in Southern California, Los Angeles Dodgers ace Tarik Skubal turned up the heat, too.The lefty hurler consistently flirted with and eventually topped 100 mph in Game 1 of the National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves on Saturday at Dodger Stadium.That set up his lethal changeup, which played a pivotal role in his retiring 15 straight batters after conceding a leadoff single. Skubal got plenty of run support, too, with the Dodgers homering three times in a 5-3 victory that staked Dave Roberts' crew to a 1-0 series lead.Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker both smashed two-run homers. Max Muncy hit a solo shot. Shohei Ohtani, who has been battling knee, biceps and neck issues, ripped a single in his first at-bat of the playoffs, yet finished 1-for-4.The Braves' runs were also the result of long balls. Sean Murphy went yard in the sixth to temporarily make it a one-run game, and Ozzie Albies provided Atlanta fans a sliver of hope in the ninth with a no-out, two-run blast.Skubal ended the afternoon with seven strikeouts — four off his signature changeup — and gave up only two hits and one run in his first playoff start for the Dodgers after they acquired the two-time reigning Cy Young Award winner from the Detroit Tigers ahead of the trade deadline.Tarik Skubal is PUMPED after retiring his 15th straight batter pic.twitter.com/DZ8mszRZIt— Talkin' Baseball (@TalkinBaseball_) October 3, 2026 The Braves began the NLDS with the same blueprint they used to finish off the Philadelphia Phillies in the wild-card round two days earlier. It offered manager Walt Weiss the start he was looking for, defensively at least.The hero of Atlanta’s winner-take-all game versus the Phillies was left-handed reliever Ray Kerr, who opened with 3 1/3 innings of shutout ball. Weiss entrusted another member of his bullpen, southpaw Dylan Dodd, with the ball to start Saturday's game against the Dodgers. Dodd delivered as well, recording three scoreless frames while tallying four strikeouts.But as soon as the Braves changed things on the bump, the game got bumpy for the NL East champs. The NL West's best feasted on Atlanta's Victor Mederos in the fourth. The righty struggled with his command from the get-go, issuing a four-pitch walk to Freddie Freeman and then hanging a cutter over the middle of the plate against Hernández. The left fielder crushed a towering, 431-foot, two-run dinger off that pitch.He watched it land from the batter's box, knowing it was gone as soon as he launched it. With that, the Dodgers were up 2-0. TEOSCAR HERNÁNDEZ LEAVES THE YARD! pic.twitter.com/fPkgA1xwKz— MLB (@MLB) October 3, 2026 The most trouble Skubal ran into came in the sixth inning. Just when he looked unhittable, he allowed a solo home run to Murphy. In total, Skubal needed 28 pitches to get through the frame, in which he walked a pair of Braves. But he preserved a 2-1 lead for L.A., which soon built a four-run cushion.In the bottom half of that inning, Hernández singled, and Kyle Tucker smacked a cathartic round-tripper off righty AJ Smith-Shawver. Hernández and Tucker both went 2-for-4 on the day.Tucker, an All-Star in four straight seasons with the Houston Astros (2022-24) and Chicago Cubs (2025) before signing a four-year, $240 million deal with L.A. in this past offseason, hit a meager.233 with the Dodgers in the regular season. He's well on his way to exorcising those demons in the playoffs.Also in the bottom of the sixth, Max Muncy recorded his 17th career postseason home run — the most in Dodgers history — by pulling a solo shot over the right-field wall to put L.A. ahead 5-1.The @Dodgers are teeing off 🚀Max Muncy blasts the third homer of the day for LA! pic.twitter.com/JNDTToh9qN— MLB (@MLB) October 3, 2026 From there, the score didn't budge until the ninth, when Albies' big fly cut Atlanta's deficit to two runs. But lefty Tanner Scott bounced back to induce back-to-back groundouts. And right-hander Evan Phillips shut the door on any potential comeback.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for in-game updates, highlights and more from Game 1 of the NLDS between the Dodgers and Braves.
